title.narrative: Ethiopia Tigray Joint Response (ETJR)

description.narrative:
A total of 3,778 beneficiaries will receive food and Shelter supports by the two local partners(EOC-DICAC and Caritas Ethiopia). 2000 people will be supported food items and 1,778 people will get Shelter Items(NFIs). All partners and their local implementing partners have agreed to follow the same five guiding rules for beneficiary selection and targeting.
Beneficiaries are selected through involvement of local government, community elders and partners, selecting the most vulnerable through agreed criteria. Selection criteria of most vulnerable are in line with cluster guidelines and include: - Female Headed Household; - Child Headed Household; - Disabled Headed Household; - Elderly Headed Household with no adults having an income;
Provide life-saving assistance to people facing severe acute needs.

Since the conflict between a federal military force and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), thousands of people’s lives has been impacted and worsening the already poor humanitarian situation. At least 222,413 people are internally displaced as a result of the conflict, while 58,334 people have fled into neighboring Sudan (UNHCR, 2020). Additionally, at least 63,000 have been displaced within Amhara and Afar (UNICEF, 2021). According to the Emergency Coordination Center (ECC) 4,5 million people need direct food assistance as a result of insecurity on imports and the harvest. Before the conflict started, a total of 507,000 already received food assistance.
Two months since the start of the conflict in Tigray, the humanitarian situation continues to critically deteriorate. Dire shortages of the most basic supplies, including food, water, fuel and cash affect the whole region, leading to a looming humanitarian catastrophe. With access to water, sanitation & health services seriously disrupted, humanitarians warned about the heightened risk of water-borne & vector-borne diseases, as well as COVID-19. The situation in and around the four refugee camps, which together host 96,000 refugees, is absolutely dire. Many people, including 5 NGO staff members, were killed during the horrific atrocities that took place during attacks (UN OCHA, 2021). Despite declaring the completion of the war, fighting continues and the situation in Tigray remains extremely volatile. Sporadic fighting in rural areas is reported on a weekly and sometimes even daily basis. The security situation is dire, especially in peripheral areas and villages around Mekelle, where looting and other incidents are still occurring. Despite the challenging security environment, humanitarians continue to deliver limited assistance with available resources and in the limited areas where access is relatively permissive.

title.narrative: The Humanitarian Response was Timely

description.narrative:
SPHERE: Communities and people affected by crisis, including the most vulnerable groups, consider that the timing of the assistance and protection they receive is adequate. DRA: timely depends on the nature of the acute crisis (slow versus sudden onset). If it is an acute sudden onset crisis a response is considered timely if we decide to respond within 48 hours and if we initiate the response within 72 hours. If it is a slow onset crisis, it is timely if we initiate the response in 3 weeks after we decide that the crisis meets the criteria of an acute crisis.
The applicable definition depends on the type of crisis (protracted versus acute). The SPHERE definition should be used in more protracted crisis where there is (more) time to conduct assessments and measure satisfaction of the response in the eyes of people affected. The DRA definition should be used for acute crises, where it is more important to initiate the response as soon as possible and look at our own processes.

description.narrative: Basic food needs: assistance, combined with beneficiaries' own resources, to international standard of 2100 kcal per person per day for the period of the action. title.narrative: ACC-R1: Number of crisis-affected people who are also involved in the design, implementation, monitoring and/or evaluation of the programme

description.narrative: Participation is defined as the involvement of crisis-affected people in one or more phases of the programme: assessment, design, implementation, monitoring or evaluation. Participation does not take place when activities are carried out in exchange for a salary of 'in-kind' payment unless the affected people are involved in decision-making processes and have an impact on decisions that affect them. Please describe in the activity description what this involvement specifically entails and in which phase of the program conflict-affected people are involved.

title.narrative: SHL-R1: Number of people having access to basic, safe and dignified shelters solutions

description.narrative: Basic, safe and dignified: - affected individuals have an minimum covered floor area of 3.5m2 per person. - all shelter solutions and materials meet locally agreed technical and performance standards and are culturally acceptable. - all household (re-)construction is in accordance with safe building practices and standards. - all household (re-)construction demonstrate involvement of the affected population and/or are culturally acceptable by the affected population.

title.narrative: ACC-R2: Number of adaptations in the design and/or implementation of the JR, as a result of the input from beneficiaries.

description.narrative: Active participation of beneficiaries could lead to concrete proposals in programme design and/or on how to improve existing implementation. In the activity description/comment field, indicate how this input from beneficiaries is gathered (planned) and at mid/end-term stage, what input was received from beneficiaries and to which adaptations this has led.
